messages:
zoe: Quick microreport from today's bring-up: evaluated 'orca-lite-8b' at fp16 / int8 / a new mixed-int5 backend across a 1.5k sample set (short chat, multi-bullet extraction, longform summarization, and numeric-normalization). Dropping a concise GTN/product handoff with recommended defaults and guardrails. Link: https://internal.redwood/bench/4901

rahul: Great. Paste the headline scorecard we can show product.

zoe: Scorecard (1.5k mixed slices):
```
metric                 | fp16    | int8    | int5   | notes
QA F1                  | 0.897   | 0.889   | 0.859  | int8 ~0.9% avg drop; int5 bigger on extraction
Exact Match (EM)       | 0.834   | 0.826   | 0.792  | extraction-sensitive
ROUGE-L (long summary)  | 0.446   | 0.436   | 0.410  | longform affected more at low precision
Latency p50 (ms)       | 108     | 121     | 135    | p95 amplified for long contexts
Latency p95 (ms)       | 305     | 356     | 412    | kv-cache interaction increases p95
Cost / 1k tokens       | $0.46   | $0.33   | $0.21  | ~28% / ~54% savings vs fp16
Throughput (req/s)     | 9.2     | 10.8    | 12.4   | int5 fastest but lower fidelity
```
Notes: Priming with a 3-token system context reduced variance for int8 on short chat. The mixed-int5 backend is promising for discovery-only endpoints but shows repeatable omissions on multi-bullet extraction and numeric unit conversions.

megan: Which extraction cases are brittle? any reproducible prompts?

zoe: Failure modes: (1) multi-bullet lists where low-frequency keys are omitted; (2) numeric normalization/units (e.g., "0.002 A -> mA"); (3) long coreference chains spanning >700 tokens. Example issue prompt: "Parse the spec and return CSV rows: id, threshold_mV, retry_limit" 0% of int5 replies missed threshold_mV on edge cases.

rahul: For GTN routing, what's your recommended default mapping and simple fallback logic? Keep it one-liner per tier.

zoe: Suggested defaults (one-liners):
- Exploratory / trial accounts -> mixed-int5 (economy) to reduce cost and increase throughput.
- Default product endpoints -> int8 (balanced) for most workloads.
- Critical extraction / compliance / longform outputs -> fp16 (premium).
Fallback rule: shadow 1% of economy/balanced traffic to fp16; if rolling EM delta > 1.5% for 20 minutes, bias 10% of traffic to fp16 and alert.

megan: Can you give a tiny router snippet we can paste into router configs?

zoe: Sure, minimal example to paste:
```
# Router predicates are pseudo-syntax for readability
routes:
  - name: premium
    predicate: tokens>800 or task=="extraction" or user_tier=="sla"
    model: orca-lite-fp16
  - name: balanced
    predicate: user_tier=="default" and tokens<=800
    model: orca-lite-int8
  - name: economy
    predicate: user_tier=="trial"
    model: orca-lite-mixed-int5
```

rahul: Nice. What runtime guardrails and tolerances should product expect?

zoe: Runtime guardrails (suggested):
- Shadowing: mirror 1% of int5/int8 queries to fp16; compute rolling deltas on EM and QA F1. Page if delta > 1.5% sustained over 20m.
- Adversarial probes: hourly batch of 200 targeted examples (multi-bullet extraction, numeric normalization, long coref). Fail-fast if EM drops >3% vs fp16.
- Lightweight signal: monitor "missing-field" smell by running a fast regexp on outputs for expected keys for extraction endpoints; if missing-field rate >0.8% for 10m, tip traffic to fp16.
- Latency guard: if int8/int5 p95 > fp16 p95 * 1.35 and error rate > baseline*1.2, throttle economy traffic.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued: canary/orca-4901-quant -> 1.5k requests over 90m. Full bench report will post to #eng-ml/bench-reports when complete.

prod-liaison: For product handoff blurb, I'll use: "Recommend tiered defaults: economy=int5 for discovery, balanced=int8 for general product, premium=fp16 for critical extraction/longform. Expect ~28% token cost savings with int8, ~54% with int5; anticipate average accuracy loss: int8 ~0.8-1.2%, int5 ~3-6% depending on workload. Require 1% shadowing and hourly adversarial checks; enable auto-fallback on sustained deltas."

megan: Product wants a one-line explainer for legal/security: any extra cautions?

zoe: One-liner: "Do not use mixed-int5 for regulated PII extraction or compliance reports; route those to premium fp16 and enable logging + deterministic seeds for auditability."

rahul: Perfect. I'll add the router snippet to GTN snippets, hook up the shadowing job, and set the canary. Will follow up with per-slice tables once canary posts.

zoe: Thanks everyone 144d

megan: Great work b50

zoe: I'll iterate on thresholds after canary metrics land.
